tasks.title: Read it all
tasks.statement: Write slurp<R: Read>(mut r: R) -> io::Result<String>: read the whole source into a string.
tasks.hint: &[u8] and Cursor implement Read; a UTF-8 error arrives as an io::Error.

tasks.title: Lines and words
tasks.statement: Write wc<R: BufRead>(r: R) -> io::Result<(usize, usize, usize)>: the number of lines, words (split_whitespace) and bytes (including line terminators) in the stream.
tasks.hint: read_line returns the number of bytes read; 0 means the end.

tasks.title: Sum of numbers from input
tasks.statement: Write sum_input<R: BufRead>(r: R) -> io::Result<i64>: the sum of integers, one per line; skip empty lines, and report an InvalidData error for invalid ones.
tasks.hint: io::Error::new(ErrorKind::InvalidData, e)

tasks.title: Copy with a transformation
tasks.statement: Write shout<R: BufRead, W: Write>(r: R, w: &mut W) -> io::Result<()>: write each input line to the output in upper case, with a "!" at the end and a newline.
tasks.hint: writeln!(w, …) writes to any Write.

tasks.title: Double write
tasks.statement: Write tee<R: Read, A: Write, B: Write>(mut r: R, a: &mut A, b: &mut B) -> io::Result<usize>: read from r in blocks of 4 bytes and write each block to both a and b; return the number of bytes.
tasks.hint: read may return fewer bytes than the buffer size, so write buf[..n].

tasks.title: Limit reading
tasks.statement: Write head(r: impl Read, n: u64) -> io::Result<String>: the first n bytes (the take method), as a string (lossy).
tasks.hint: r.take(n).read_to_end(&mut buf)

tasks.title: Joining streams
tasks.statement: Write joined(a: &str, b: &str) -> String: read two sources one after another through chain as one, and return the result.
tasks.hint: Read::chain joins two sources.

tasks.title: Fixed-length header
tasks.statement: Write read_header<R: Read>(mut r: R) -> io::Result<(u16, u32)>: read 6 bytes, two bytes of u16 and four bytes of u32, in little-endian order; if the data is too short, return an UnexpectedEof error (read_exact).
tasks.hint: from_le_bytes for each field.

tasks.title: Binary write
tasks.statement: Write write_u32s<W: Write>(w: &mut W, v: &[u32]) -> io::Result<()>: write the numbers in big-endian order one after another (to_be_bytes).
tasks.hint: x.to_be_bytes() returns [u8; 4].

tasks.title: File tail
tasks.statement: Write tail_bytes<R: Read + Seek>(mut r: R, n: u64) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>>: the last n bytes (or everything, if there is less data). Use Seek::seek(SeekFrom::End(…)).
tasks.hint: seek(End(0)) returns the size.

tasks.title: Patch at an offset
tasks.statement: Write patch<S: Read + Write + Seek>(mut s: S, pos: u64, data: &[u8]) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>>: write data starting at position pos and return the whole content after the patch.
tasks.hint: A cursor over a vector implements Read, Write and Seek at once.

tasks.title: BufWriter
tasks.statement: Write write_squares<W: Write>(w: W, n: u32) -> io::Result<()>: wrapping w in a BufWriter, write the squares of the numbers 1…n, one per line.
tasks.hint: BufWriter::new(w) and flush() at the end.

tasks.title: read_until
tasks.statement: Write records<R: BufRead>(mut r: R) -> io::Result<Vec<String>>: records separated by the character ";" (read_until); the separator is not part of a record, and empty records are skipped.
tasks.hint: read_until includes the separator in the buffer, so remove it.

tasks.title: Read a grid
tasks.statement: Write read_grid<R: BufRead>(r: R) -> io::Result<Vec<Vec<i32>>>: the first line is "N M", then N lines of M numbers separated by spaces. If there are not enough lines or numbers, return an InvalidData error.
tasks.hint: Define a closure bad() to create the error.

tasks.title: Parts of a path
tasks.statement: Write describe(p: &str) -> String: «каталог=…, имя=…, расширение=…» (directory, name, extension; use parent, file_stem, extension; a missing part is "-").
tasks.hint: Path::new(p).parent(), file_stem(), extension() all return Option.

tasks.title: Joining paths
tasks.statement: Write build_path(parts: &[&str]) -> String: join the parts into a path with PathBuf::push (an absolute part replaces everything before it); the result is a string. For ["/a", "b", "c.txt"] this is "/a/b/c.txt".
tasks.hint: push with an absolute path replaces what has accumulated.

tasks.title: Change the extension
tasks.statement: Write to_bak(name: &str) -> String: replace the extension with "bak" (with_extension), and for a name without an extension, add it.
tasks.hint: with_extension replaces the last extension.

tasks.title: File: write and read
tasks.statement: Write roundtrip(text: &str) -> io::Result<String>: write text to a temporary file in the std::env::temp_dir() directory (with the process id in the name), read it back, delete the file and return what was read.
tasks.hint: fs::write, fs::read_to_string, fs::remove_file.

tasks.title: Appending to a file
tasks.statement: Write append_lines(lines: &[&str]) -> io::Result<usize>: in a temporary file (std::env::temp_dir(), with the process id in the name) append the lines one by one (OpenOptions append) using two separate opens; return the number of lines in the file; delete the file.
tasks.hint: OpenOptions::new().append(true).create(true).open(&p)

tasks.title: Walking a directory
tasks.statement: Write make_and_list() -> io::Result<Vec<String>>: in a temporary directory (temp_dir plus a name with the process id) create a directory with the (empty) files c.txt, a.txt, b.log, read it with read_dir, return the names in alphabetical order and remove the directory with all its contents (remove_dir_all).
tasks.hint: read_dir returns an iterator of io::Result<DirEntry>; the order is undefined, so sort.

tasks.title: Kind of error
tasks.statement: Write open_kind(path: &str) -> String: try to open the file; return "ok" on success, «нет файла» for NotFound, «нет доступа» for PermissionDenied and «ошибка» for anything else.
tasks.hint: e.kind() returns an ErrorKind. A directory can be opened for reading, but it cannot be read.

tasks.title: Your own error type
tasks.statement: Declare enum AppError { Io(io::Error), Parse(std::num::ParseIntError) } with derive(Debug) and implement From for both variants. Then the function read_num(r: impl Read) -> Result<i32, AppError> reads a string and parses the number with a single ? at each step.
tasks.hint: impl From<…> for AppError, with the body AppError::Variant(e).

tasks.title: Line numbers
tasks.statement: Write number_lines<R: BufRead, W: Write>(r: R, w: &mut W) -> io::Result<()>: write each line with a number (starting at 1) in the format «   1: текст» (number right-aligned in a field of width 4, then the line itself instead of «текст»).
tasks.hint: enumerate() over lines().

tasks.title: grep
tasks.statement: Write grep<R: BufRead>(r: R, pat: &str, ignore_case: bool) -> io::Result<Vec<(usize, String)>>: the numbers (from 1) and texts of the lines that contain pat (case-insensitive when ignore_case is set).
tasks.hint: Convert both the pattern and the line to lower case.

tasks.title: CSV column
tasks.statement: Write column_sum<R: BufRead>(r: R, col: usize) -> io::Result<f64>: the sum of the numbers in column col (from 0) of lines like «a,1.5,b»; the first line is a header and is skipped; empty fields count as zero; a non-numeric field is an InvalidData error.
tasks.hint: split(',').nth(col) is the field you need.

tasks.title: Hex dump
tasks.statement: Write hexdump(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<String>: lines of 8 bytes each, «offset (4 hex digits): bytes separated by spaces» (the last line may be shorter): «0000: 48 65 6c …».
tasks.hint: chunks(8) and enumerate; the offset is i * 8.

tasks.title: Running a program
tasks.statement: Write echo_via_shell(word: &str) -> String: run the command "echo" with the argument word through std::process::Command and return its output without the trailing newline. (The sandbox has /bin/echo.)
tasks.hint: Command::new("echo").arg(word).output()

tasks.title: How many bytes were printed
tasks.statement: Write counted(f: impl Fn(&mut dyn Write)) -> usize: call f, passing it a vector of bytes as the Write, and return the number of bytes written.
tasks.hint: &mut Vec<u8> coerces to &mut dyn Write.

tasks.title: Lines in reverse order
tasks.statement: Write reverse_lines<R: BufRead, W: Write>(r: R, w: &mut W) -> io::Result<()>: write the input lines in reverse order (one per line).
tasks.hint: lines().collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?

tasks.title: Parsing arguments
tasks.statement: Write parse_args(args: &[&str]) -> (bool, Option<String>, Vec<String>): the flag "-v" (verbose), the option "-o <file>" (output) and the remaining words as positional arguments, like simple command-line utilities.
tasks.hint: Iterate over the arguments: after "-o" take the next item.
